items.title: How fast does 'manually check every pair for a hidden cycle' grow as services are added?
items.description: To be truly sure no cycle exists just by eyeballing a spreadsheet, every pair of services is a potential piece of a loop worth cross-checking. That count grows combinatorially with the number of services. A graph script's cost, by contrast, stays roughly proportional to the number of services and their listed edges -- it doesn't care how tangled the web gets. Drag the slider to L1's own 14 services and see how many manual cross-checks that already implies, then push toward a larger platform.

params.name: numServices
params.label: Number of services in the dependency web

items.compute: const n = params.numServices; const pairsToCheck = (n * (n - 1)) / 2; return { pairsToCheck };

outputs.label: Pairs of services to manually cross-check for a hidden cycle
